tiles.label: Totals
tiles.visitorsSub: Unique people. Someone visiting several times in a day counts once.
tiles.pagesSub: Average pages viewed per visit. Higher means more people keep browsing.
tiles.bounceSub: The "bounce rate": share of people who leave after the first page. Lower is better.
tiles.durationSub: Roughly how long from arriving to leaving (average per visit).

more.note: Countries are guessed from the connection's location. Readers on a VPN or proxy count as wherever that endpoint is, so treat this as a rough guide.

posts.heading: Per post
posts.note: "Avg. time" is the average from opening the post to leaving (time in a background tab doesn't count); "Reading time" is estimated from the word count. A big gap between the two means most people only read the beginning. "Scrolled" is the furthest point reached as a share of the post; jumping to the bottom or skipping ahead via the table of contents also counts, so it runs higher than what was actually read. All language versions of a post are combined; hearts and comments are all-time, not limited to this period.
posts.empty: Nobody has read a post in this period yet.

sources.heading: Where they came from, and what they saw first
sources.note: "Direct" means no referrer: bookmarks, typing the URL, or links opened from some messaging apps (LINE and Discord sometimes drop the referrer).

search.heading: What people searched on Google
search.setup: Search Console isn't connected: mount the service account key into the backend in docker-compose.yml and set GSC_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE (see backend/src/handlers/search_console.rs).
search.note: "Impressions" is how often this site appeared in search results; "Clicks" is how often someone clicked through. Google's data lags two or three days, so the last few days look low.
search.empty: No search data for this period.

reactions.heading: Hearts and reactions received
reactions.note: Every heart, emoji reaction, comment like and thought like is logged, and so is every undo. No identity or IP is stored: the country comes from Cloudflare, and the source is the site the reader came from.
reactions.site: Left a mark on the home page
reactions.commentThought: Liked a comment on the thought "{{title}}"
reactions.commentMessages: Liked a comment on the guestbook
reactions.commentDeleted: Liked a comment that was later deleted
reactions.thoughtUnlike: Took back a like on the thought "{{title}}"
reactions.thoughtUndislike: Took back a dislike on the thought "{{title}}"
reactions.totals: Hearts on posts: {{hearts}} · Marks on the home page: {{marks}} (totals only, no details)

setup.intro: Plausible isn't connected. The backend needs a Stats API key:
setup.step1: Open Plausible, click your avatar (top right) → Account Settings → API Keys → New API Key, and choose Stats API as the type.
setup.step2: Add the key to .env.backend on the server: PLAUSIBLE_API_KEY=… (if the site name in Plausible isn't koimsurai.com, also add PLAUSIBLE_SITE_ID=…)
setup.step3: Restart the backend: docker compose up -d backend-rs
setup.keyNote: The key stays on the backend and never reaches the frontend code.
